subject: maths
title: Chance: Will Happen, Might Happen or Won’t Happen
seo_title: Year 1 Chance Worksheets: Will, Might or Won’t Happen (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Identify outcomes of familiar events involving chance and describe them using everyday language, such as “will happen”, “won’t happen” or “might happen”
meta_desc: Free Year 1 maths worksheets on chance for the Australian Curriculum: say if everyday events will happen, might happen or won’t happen, find what you can get on a spinner or from a bag of counters, choose which colour is more likely, and toss coins and roll dice. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Will happen means we are sure. Might happen means it can happen, but we are not sure. Won’t happen means it can’t happen.
key_sub: If all the parts of a spinner are red, you will get red. If some are red, you might get red. If none are red, you won’t get red. Always look at what is in the bag first.
body_html:
Three chance words

Some things we are sure about. Some things we are not sure about. We use three phrases.

WordsMeaningExample
will happenWe are sure it happens.The sun will set tonight.
might happenIt can happen, but we are not sure.It might rain tomorrow.
won’t happenIt can’t happen.It won’t snow at the beach in summer.
Will, might or won’t?

Our team plays footy today. Will we win?

A team can win or lose. We are not sure.

Answer: Our team might win.

Spinners

Look at the colours on the spinner. If all the parts are red, you will get red. If some parts are red, you might get red. If no parts are red, you won’t get red.

Example

Will you get red?

Most parts are red, but there is a blue part.

Answer: No. You might get red.

Bags of counters

Look in the bag before you answer. You can only pick a colour that is in the bag. The colour with more counters is more likely.

Example

Can you pick blue?

There is 1 blue counter. It is in the bag.

Answer: Yes. You might pick blue.

Coins and dice

A coin can land on heads or tails. A dice can show 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6. Every number has the same chance. You won’t roll a 7.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Saying “will” when it only might happenUse “will” only when you are sure
Saying “won’t” when there is only a little of a colourIf it is there at all, it might happen
Not looking in the bagCheck which colours are in the bag first
Choosing your favourite colourCount the parts or counters of each colour
Thinking 6 is harder to roll than 1Every number on a dice has the same chance

faq.q: What do Year 1 students learn about chance in Australia?
faq.a: The Australian Curriculum (AC9M1P01) asks Year 1 students to talk about familiar events and say whether they will happen, won’t happen or might happen. For example, the sun will set tonight, but it won’t snow at the beach in summer.

faq.q: What is the difference between “will happen” and “might happen”?
faq.a: “Will happen” means we are sure, like Tuesday coming after Monday. “Might happen” means it can happen but we are not sure, like rain tomorrow.

faq.q: How can I teach chance to a 6-year-old at home?
faq.a: Use a bag of coloured blocks or a homemade spinner. Ask “Will you get red, might you get red, or won’t you get red?” and then try it to see.

faq.q: Why does my child say a colour won’t come up when it is on the spinner?
faq.a: Many children think a small part can never be landed on. Spin a few times together and show that if a colour is there at all, it might happen.

sets.title: Will happen, might happen or won’t happen?

items.q: A hot summer day at the beach. What won’t happen?
items.e: Summer at the beach is warm. Snow never falls on a hot summer beach. So it won’t happen.

items.q: A hot summer day at the beach. What might happen?
c: It will snow on the sand.
The sea will turn to milk.
items.e: Dolphins live in the sea. You see one on some days, but not every day. So it might happen. The other things won’t happen.

items.q: It is night. What will happen?
c: The sun will shine all night.
items.e: Every night the sky is dark. It will happen. A frog or rain might happen, but not for sure.

items.q: It is night. What won’t happen?
items.e: The sun does not shine at night. That won’t happen. The other things might happen.

items.q: Which one will happen?
items.e: The sun sets every evening, so it will happen. You might see a whale, but not for sure. Snow in class and a talking dog won’t happen.

items.q: Dark clouds fill the sky. What might happen?
c: The clouds will turn into cats.
items.e: Dark clouds often bring rain, but not always. So it might rain. The other things won’t happen.

items.q: It is a school day. What will happen?
c: A cow will be your teacher.
items.e: The school bell rings every school day, so it will happen. A sticker or cricket might happen.

items.q: It is a school day. What won’t happen?
c: A fish will teach the class.
items.e: A fish can’t teach. That won’t happen. Reading, painting and eating an apple might happen.

items.q: Mia is 6 today. What will happen?
c: It might rain at the party.
items.e: Every year you get 1 year older. 6 + 1 = 7, so it will happen. You can’t get younger, so 3 won’t happen.

items.q: Mia is 6 today. What might happen?
items.e: A puppy is a gift Mia might get, or might not. So it might happen. Being 7 next year will happen. The other two won’t happen.

items.q: At the park. What might happen?
items.e: Kookaburras live in many Australian parks. You might see one, or you might not. The other things won’t happen.

items.q: At the park. What won’t happen?
c: You might go on the swings.
items.e: A tree can’t fly. That won’t happen. The other things might happen.

items.q: Isla says, “It will rain tomorrow.” Which is better?
items.e: We can’t be sure about rain tomorrow. It may rain, or it may not. So say “might”, not “will”.

items.q: Leo says, “It might snow at the beach in summer.” Which is better?
c: It might snow at the beach in summer.
The sea will freeze in summer.
It won’t snow at the beach in summer.
It will snow at the beach in summer.
items.e: A summer beach is hot. Snow can’t fall there. So it won’t happen. “Might” is not right.

items.q: Jack says, “The sun might set tonight.” Which is better?
c: The sun will set at lunch time.
items.e: The sun sets every evening. We are sure, so say “will”, not “might”.

items.q: Our footy team plays today. Which is right?
items.e: A team can win or lose. We can’t be sure, so our team might win. Both teams can’t win.

items.q: Today is Monday. Which is right?
items.e: Tuesday always comes after Monday. We are sure, so say “will”.

items.q: Which is right?
c: A cow might jump over the Moon.
A cow won’t jump over the Moon.
A cow will jump over the Moon.
items.e: The Moon is very, very far away. A cow can’t jump that high. So it won’t happen.

items.q: Ruby drops an egg on the floor. What will happen?
c: The egg will turn into a chick.
items.e: An egg shell is thin. When it hits the hard floor, it breaks. So it will happen.

items.q: An icy pole is left in the hot sun. What will happen?
c: It will turn into a lolly.
items.e: The hot sun melts ice. So the icy pole will melt. It won’t get bigger or colder.

items.q: You spin it. Which is right?
items.e: All the parts are red. The arrow must land on red. So you will get red.

items.q: You spin it. Which is right?
items.e: Half is red and half is blue. The arrow can land on either one. So you might get red.

items.q: You spin it. Which is right?
items.e: There is no green part. The arrow can’t land on green. So you won’t get green.

items.q: You spin it. Which is right?
items.e: Most parts are blue. But there is 1 red part, so the arrow could land on red. So you might get blue. It is not “will”.

items.q: You spin it. Which is right?
items.e: Every part is yellow. You will get yellow. There is no blue.

items.q: You spin it. Which is right?
items.e: Only 1 part is red. But it is there, so the arrow can land on it. You might get red. It is not “won’t”.

items.q: You spin it. Which is right?
items.e: The numbers are 1, 2, 3 and 4. There is no 5. So you won’t get 5.

items.q: You spin it. Which is right?
items.e: 4 is on the spinner, so you might get it. A big number is not harder to get.

items.q: You spin it. Which is right?
items.e: Every part has a 2. The arrow must land on 2. So you will get 2.

items.q: Which colour will you get?
items.e: Every part is green. So you will get green.

items.q: Which colour won’t you get?
items.e: The spinner has red, blue and yellow. There is no green. So you won’t get green.

items.q: Which colour won’t you get?
items.e: Look at the spinner. It has green, purple and yellow. There is no red.

items.q: Which number won’t you get?
items.e: The numbers go from 1 to 6. There is no 7. So you won’t get 7.

items.q: Which spinner will land on red?
items.e: Spinner B is all red. It must land on red. Spinner D is mostly red, but it has a blue part. So D might land on red.

items.q: Which spinner won’t land on red?
items.e: Spinner D has no red part. So it won’t land on red. Spinner B has 1 red part, so it might.

items.q: Which spinner might land on red?
items.e: Spinner D has red parts and blue parts. It might land on red, or it might land on blue. B will land on red. A and C won’t.

items.q: Leo says, “I will get blue.” Is he right?
items.e: Half the spinner is red. The arrow might land on red. So Leo might get blue. His favourite colour does not change the spinner.

items.q: Amelia says, “I won’t get yellow. It is too small.” Is she right?
items.e: There is 1 yellow part. The arrow can land on it. So she might get yellow. It is not “won’t”.

items.q: You spin it. Which is right?
items.e: There is 1 yellow part out of 4. The arrow can land on it, or on another colour. So you might get yellow.

items.q: You spin it. Which is right?
items.e: Every part is purple. There is no green. So you won’t get green.

sets.title: Bags of counters: what could you pick?

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: Every counter is red. You will pick red.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: There are red and blue counters. You could pick either one. So you might pick blue.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: Look in the bag. There are red and yellow counters. There is no green. So you won’t pick green.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: There is only 1 red counter. But it is in the bag, so you could pick it. You might pick red.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: Most counters are green. But there is 1 red counter. So you might pick green. It is not “will”.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: There are yellow and purple counters. You could pick a purple one. So you might pick yellow.

items.q: Which colour will you pick?
items.e: Every counter is yellow. So you will pick yellow.

items.q: Which colour won’t you pick?
items.e: The bag has red, blue and yellow counters. There is no green. So you won’t pick green.

items.q: Which colour won’t you pick?
items.e: The bag has green, purple and blue. There is no red. So you won’t pick red. There is 1 blue, so you might pick blue.

items.q: Mia wants a green counter. Can she get one?
c: Yes, if she shuts her eyes.
items.e: Look in the bag first. There are only red and blue counters. No green means she won’t get green.

items.q: Kai wants a red counter. Can he get one?
items.e: There is 1 red counter in the bag. Kai could pick it. So he might get red.

items.q: Ava takes out all the blue counters. Then she picks one. Which is right?
items.e: After the blue counters come out, only red counters are left. So she will pick red.

items.q: Noah puts 2 green counters in the bag. Then he picks one. Which is right?
items.e: Now the bag has red and green counters. So he might pick green. Before, green was “won’t”.

items.q: Which bag will give you red?
items.e: Bag D has only red counters. You will pick red. Bag C has a yellow counter, so red might happen there.

items.q: Which bag won’t give you blue?
items.e: Bag B has yellow and green counters. There is no blue. So it won’t give you blue.

items.q: Which bag might give you yellow?
items.e: Only bag B has yellow counters, and it has red ones too. So you might pick yellow from bag B.

items.q: Grace says, “I will pick red. Red is my favourite.” Is she right?
items.e: The bag has blue counters too. Her favourite colour does not change what she picks. So she might pick red.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: There are 2 yellow counters. You could pick one, or a red or blue one. So you might pick yellow.

items.q: Isla picks 2 counters. What will happen?
c: She might get a blue one.
items.e: Every counter is red. Any 2 counters she picks will be red.

items.q: Cooper wants a yellow counter. What can he do?
c: Put a yellow one in the bag.
items.e: There is no yellow in the bag, so he won’t get yellow. Picking again or shaking does not help. He must put a yellow counter in.

items.q: Which colour are you more likely to get?
items.e: 3 parts are red. Only 1 part is blue. More red means red is more likely.

items.q: Which colour are you more likely to get?
items.e: 3 parts are yellow and 1 part is green. Yellow covers more, so yellow is more likely.

items.q: Which colour are you more likely to get?
items.e: 2 parts are red and 2 parts are blue. The parts are the same size. So they are the same.

items.q: Which colour are you more likely to pick?
items.e: There are 6 blue counters and 2 red counters. More blue means blue is more likely.

items.q: Which colour are you less likely to pick?
items.e: There are only 2 yellow counters and 6 green ones. Fewer yellow means yellow is less likely.

items.q: Which colour are you more likely to pick?
items.e: 3 red and 3 blue. The same number, so they are the same.

items.q: Which colour are you less likely to get?
items.e: Only 1 part is purple. 5 parts are green. So purple is less likely.

items.q: Which number are you more likely to get?
items.e: 3 parts have a 1. Only 1 part has a 2. So 1 is more likely.

items.q: Which is more likely, 1 or 4?
items.e: 1 and 4 each have 1 part. The parts are the same size. So they are the same. A bigger number is not harder to get.

items.q: Which colour are you most likely to pick?
items.e: Count each colour: red 4, blue 2, yellow 1. Red has the most, so red is most likely.

items.q: Which colour are you least likely to pick?
items.e: Count each colour: red 4, blue 2, yellow 1. Yellow has the fewest, so yellow is least likely.

items.q: Harper loves purple. Which colour is she more likely to get?
items.e: 3 parts are green and only 1 is purple. Her favourite colour does not change the spinner. Green is more likely.

items.q: Jack wants blue. What is more likely?
items.e: Look in the bag: 5 red and 1 blue. Wanting blue does not help. Red is more likely.

items.q: Which spinner is best for getting red?
items.e: Spinner C has 3 red parts out of 4. That is the most red. Spinner D has no red at all.

items.q: Which spinner is worst for getting yellow?
items.e: Spinner C has only 1 yellow part. The others have more yellow. So C is worst for yellow.

items.q: Which bag is best for picking blue?
items.e: Each bag has 6 counters. Bag C has 5 blue counters. That is the most blue.

items.q: In which bag are red and blue the same?
items.e: Bag B has 3 red and 3 blue. The same number of each, so they are the same.

items.q: Ethan puts 3 more red counters in. Which colour is more likely now?
items.e: Red: 2 + 3 = 5. Blue: 2. 5 is more than 2, so red is now more likely.

items.q: Summer at the beach. Which is more likely?
items.e: Summer days at the beach are usually hot. Snow and frost won’t happen there in summer.

items.q: The sky is full of dark clouds. Which is more likely?
items.e: Dark clouds often bring rain. So rain is more likely.

items.q: You toss a coin. Which is right?
items.e: A coin can land on heads or tails. So you might get heads.

items.q: You toss a coin. What can you get?
items.e: A coin has 2 sides: heads and tails. It can land on either side.

items.q: You roll a dice. Which number won’t you get?
items.e: A dice has 1 to 6 dots. There is no 7. So you won’t get 7.

items.q: You roll a dice. Which is right?
items.e: 6 is on the dice. It might come up, or another number might. So you might get 6.

items.q: You roll a dice. What will happen?
items.e: Every face has 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 dots. One of them must come up. So that will happen.

items.q: You roll a dice. Which is right?
items.e: The dice only goes up to 6. There is no 9. So you won’t get 9.

items.q: Noah says, “6 is hard to get. It is a big number.” Is he right?
c: No. 6 and 1 have the same chance.
items.e: Each number is on 1 face. So every number has the same chance. Big numbers are not harder.

items.q: Which is right?
c: Heads and tails have the same chance.
items.e: A coin has 1 heads side and 1 tails side. So heads and tails have the same chance.

items.q: Kai gets heads 3 times. He tosses again. Which is right?
c: He might get heads or tails.
items.e: A coin does not remember. Each toss, heads and tails have the same chance. So he might get either one.

items.q: Harper says, “I will get heads. Heads is lucky.” Is she right?
items.e: No side is lucky. The coin might land on heads or tails. So she might get heads.

items.q: The umpire tosses a coin before the footy. Our captain calls heads. Which is right?
c: Our captain won’t win the toss.
Our captain will win the toss.
Our captain might win the toss.
items.e: The coin might land on heads, or on tails. So our captain might win. Both can’t win.

items.q: Leo needs a 6 to start the game. He rolls a dice. Which is right?
items.e: 6 is on the dice, so he might get it. He might get another number too. There is no 10.

items.q: At the school fete lucky dip, the yellow ball wins a big prize. Ava picks one ball. Which is right?
items.e: There is 1 yellow ball. Ava could pick it, but there are lots of red ones too. So she might pick yellow.

items.q: The teacher picks one name from the hat. Which is right?
items.e: Leo’s name is in the hat with 3 other names. So Leo might be picked. Ruby’s name is not in the hat, so she won’t be picked.

items.q: Ruby’s name is not in the hat. Which is right?
items.e: Only names in the hat can be picked. Ruby’s name is not there. So she won’t be picked.

items.q: The canteen has 4 red and 2 yellow icy poles. Chloe takes one without looking. Which is more likely?
items.e: There are 4 red and 2 yellow. More red means red is more likely. There are no green ones.

items.q: Ruby picks a sock in the dark. Which is right?
c: She will get a green sock.
She might get a red sock.
She won’t get a red sock.
She will get a red sock.
items.e: There are red socks and blue socks. In the dark she could get either one. So she might get red.

items.q: 6 children run a race. Jack is one of them. Which is right?
items.e: Any of the 6 children could win. We can’t be sure it is Jack. So Jack might win.

items.q: It is a cold winter day in Hobart. The sky is grey. Which is right?
c: It will be a hot summer day.
items.e: Grey clouds can bring rain, but not always. So it might rain. It is winter, so it won’t be a summer day.

items.q: The canteen has only yellow icy poles left. Liam takes one. Which is right?
c: He will get a yellow one.
He won’t get a yellow one.
He might get a blue one.
He might get a red one.
items.e: Every icy pole left is yellow. So he will get a yellow one.
